answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cost cut, so the lowest-cost path on the primary line is the priority. memory_c2 documents a prior successful switch to a low-cost primary vendor with accurate invoicing, which directly supports switch_primary_vendor as the lever most likely to hit the savings target. memory_c6 confirms multi-year commitments can unlock volume pricing — relevant because the current contract does not auto-renew and we have only one decision this cycle, so the new arrangement must be structured to capture volume pricing rather than a spot purchase. The assembly line is running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, which is the dominant risk; switching primary vendors mid-tension without a guarded ramp would transfer delivery risk onto an unproven configuration. A small_guarded_test scopes the switch narrowly enough to preserve throughput while still extracting cost, with an explicit fallback path. I am holding the switch until I have read the archived source for memory_c2 (to confirm invoicing accuracy and onboarding speed held under load) and memory_c6 (to confirm the volume-pricing terms did not narrow service scope in a way that would raise delivery risk). I am not pre-committing to renew_incumbent, negotiate_terms, add_second_source, or defer_decision here even though each has supporting memory, because under an 18% cut a renewal or deferral alone is unlikely to close the gap and adding a second source without switching primary leaves the savings on the table.
